items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The helper `punycode(domain)` has a clear name and a docstring, and its call sites read naturally. It sits at the end of encoding.py, after DEFAULT_LOCALE_ENCODING, which is a minor placement nit.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One shared helper is used across message.py and utils.py. But the domain is converted twice: in get_fqdn and again in `make_msgid(domain=punycode(str(DNS_NAME)))`, the second only to suit the test patch. sanitize_address keeps a redundant `domain.encode('ascii')` try block.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and there are no magic constants. A hostname with an invalid IDNA label would raise UnicodeError, which matches the reference behavior.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` converts at the source for every encoding. ASCII names pass through unchanged, so the extra punycode() at make_msgid does no harm. No try/except hides failures.
